requirement: A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.
rationale:
The requirement is implemented and tested, and I found no gaps.

**Implementation**
- `colon_fence` in `src/lib.rs` (about lines 541–548) accepts any line with at most 3 leading spaces and 3 or more colons. It returns the colon count and the rest of the line.
- `definition_blocks` (`src/lib.rs` 467–537) records the opener's `fence_length`. It ends the body at the first later line that meets all three conditions:
  - it is not inside a Markdown code block, so a closer inside a fenced code example is ignored;
  - its colon count is at least `fence_length`;
  - nothing but whitespace follows the colons.
- A shorter colon-only line therefore stays in the body. A nested `:::{note}` also stays in the body, because it has a non-empty suffix and fewer colons.
- `src/evidence.rs` (about line 296–319) takes the requirement text from `content[block.body_start..block.body_end]`. `src/index.rs` also uses `colon_fence` and `>= fence_length` for the index marker, so it handles long fences the same way.

**Tests**
- `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers` in `src/evidence.rs` is tagged `{test}requirements.ci.fence_lengths`.
  - It tries the opener/closer pairs `::::`/`::::`, `::::`/`:::::` and `:::::::`/`::::::::`.
  - Each body holds a nested `:::{note}…:::` directive and text after it.
  - It checks that the full body is recognised as the requirement text, with no validation errors.
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` in `src/evidence.rs` is also tagged with this requirement.
  - It covers a `:::` line inside a fenced code example not ending the body.
  - It also checks that text after the real closer is excluded.
- `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` in `src/lib.rs` checks the exact body, the `closed` flag and the text after the block for `::::{req}` with a nested `:::` directive.
  - It is tagged `requirements.ci.span` rather than this requirement, but it exercises the same behaviour.
- `marker_accepts_long_fences_and_ignores_examples` in `src/index.rs` covers long fences for the index marker.

**Coverage**
- Together the tests cover:
  - three or more colons at the opener;
  - closers of equal and greater length;
  - a shorter nested fence staying in the body;
  - a closer inside a code example being ignored.
- There is no dedicated test for a too-short closer leaving the block unclosed. The nested `:::` in the body tests already exercises that logic.
